slices.focus: An experienced caseworker's resignation pushes Nadia to build peer-shadowing and overflow coverage instead of scrambling.
slices.summary: After an experienced caseworker gives notice following a brutal summer, Nadia pushes leadership to approve a peer-shadowing and overflow-coverage plan rather than just posting the job and stretching remaining staff. She plans to draft a task priority hierarchy first (time-sensitive intake vs. deferrable work), then a rotating shadow calendar, then a simple coverage protocol for absences. She will use an upcoming vacation as a practice run with a three-question debrief.
open_loops: Draft task priority hierarchy (what must be protected vs. what can pause)
Design simple coverage protocol for absences
Test plan using upcoming vacation as practice run
Debrief with three questions: what got covered smoothly, what confused people, what depended on one person's memory
decisions: Nadia shifted her supervisory focus from the school-district welcome-center expansion to a peer-shadowing and overflow-c
